To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed a large and diverse association panel in grapevine that is suitable for genetic studies.

we designed a diversity grapevine panel that adequately captures most of the genetic diversity and phenotypic variation existing within the Vassal collection and is powerful enough to detect associations between causal loci with high effect and agronomic traits.
we have designed a large and diverse grapevine panel for association studies and that this panel has the potential for association analysis of traits with high heritability and strong effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic diversity and linkage disequilibrium in the largest grapevine panel worldwide, and the power of this panel to detect associations between phenotypic and genotypic data.
the genetic diversity, the linkage disequilibrium, and the power of a newly designed large grapevine diversity panel.
the design of a panel of grapevine cultivars, with the assessment of the genetic diversity, the linkage disequilibrium, and the power of the panel for association mapping.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this panel constitutes an excellent resource for genetic association in grapevine, with the caveat that it should be used with care when the aim is to detect QTL with small effect.
the panel designed in this study is a powerful tool to detect genetic markers associated with quantitative traits in the context of GWAS in grapevine.

this study provides a new, highly useful, and highly valuable genetic resource for association studies in grapevines, which deserves dissemination to various field and greenhouse trials for gaining further insight into the genetic regulation of various agronomic traits and the interactions between these traits and the environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Vassal association panel is the first one to be used for association mapping in grapevine.
our panel is well suited for the detection of associations between traits with moderate to high heritability and causal loci explaining a large part of the total variance.
the panel was designed to represent most of V. vinifera diversity and that the panel has a good power to detect QTLs with high broad-sens heritability and moderate effect size.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a panel with 279 cultivars, with a limited relatedness and including most of the genetic diversity of the Vassal collection, is adequate to capture most of the diversity existing in the whole collection.
a diversity panel can be built from a collection of germplasm, and that this panel can be assessed for its power in a genome wide association study, even if it is not genotyped on the whole genome.
a diversity panel of grapevine can be designed to reflect the whole germplasm diversity and be used for association studies.
